q: A job is completed during the month, its cost sheet is struck and its cost is billed to the Depreciation Reserve Fund through a transfer entry. In the Outturn Statement (W.1204), this job will be shown in:

options.A: Part II, because it was billed to the DRF
options.B: Part I, as a job completed and adjusted in the month
options.C: Part II, because the cost sheet was struck only this month
options.D: Neither part, because DRF work is shown separately

e: Part I covers works completed and adjustable in the month of account; once billed out, the amount is credited out of WMS to the final head.

q: At month-end a wagon POH job is physically finished, but the outturn voucher has been received and accepted without yet being accounted for, and adjustment is still awaited. How is this job treated in W.1204 and in WMS?

options.A: It stays in Part II and forms part of the WMS closing balance
options.B: It is shown in Part I and credited out of WMS
options.C: It is written off from WMS as the work is physically complete
options.D: It is transferred to Stores Suspense pending adjustment

e: Vouchers received and accepted but not yet accounted for remain outstanding in Part II until adjusted; completed-but-unbilled work is one of the only two components of the WMS closing balance.

q: A gang loses three hours of productive work because of a power failure in the shop. The wages for this lost time are to be booked. The correct booking is:

options.A: To the job on which the gang was working when the power failed
options.B: To the next job the gang takes up after power is restored
options.C: To the Shop On-Cost Work Order, from where it is absorbed over all jobs
options.D: As a deduction from the gang's wages for the month

e: Idle time — wages for time lost waiting for material or work, machine breakdown or power failure — is charged to the Shop On-Cost Work Order and is never debited to a job.

q: After completing a job, a shop finds surplus material and scrap lying on the shop floor and returns them to the stores depot. In the WMS account, this return appears:

options.A: On the debit side, as additional material consumed
options.B: On the debit side, as a direct purchase by the CWM
options.C: Nowhere, because returned material is not accounted for in WMS
options.D: On the credit side, at the returned / scrap value

e: Material returned to stores is no longer workshop expenditure; in the specimen account it is credited to WMS (Rs 15,250) at returned / scrap value.

q: The CWM purchases material directly for a workshop activity, and the material never passes through the stores depot or the Stores Suspense. Its cost is accounted for by:

options.A: Debiting the Stores Suspense first and then transferring it to WMS
options.B: Debiting WMS straight, as a direct / local purchase
options.C: Debiting the final revenue head directly, bypassing WMS
options.D: Crediting WMS, as the purchase is made outside the depot

e: Direct purchases made by the CWM for workshop activities are debited straight to WMS; in the specimen month they amount to Rs 15,000 within the material group.

q: The Workshop Accounts Officer has to render, for each workshop, the monthly suspense position of WMS showing the opening balance, the debit heads, the credit heads and the closing balance. The statement he prepares is the:

options.B: Outturn Statement, Form W.1204

e: The suspense position is rendered monthly by the WAO for each workshop in the WMS Account Current, Form W.1215.

q: The shops have closed the job cards for a completed job and the Costing Section has struck its cost sheet. The next step by which the job's cost leaves WMS and reaches the final head is:

options.A: The job is entered again in the Workshop General Register as a fresh charge
options.B: The WAO debits the job's cost to the Shop On-Cost Work Order
options.C: The WAO posts the Outturn Statement (W.1204) and a JV / transfer entry credits WMS and debits the final head
options.D: The cost sheet is sent to the stores depot for pricing into the priced ledger

e: On completion the flow is: job cards closed, Cost Sheet (W.934) struck, Outturn Statement (W.1204) posted by the WAO from the WGR, and a JV/transfer entry adjusts the outturn out of WMS to Capital, DRF, Revenue or Stores Suspense.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense (WMS):
1. WMS is a Capital Suspense account under Plan Head 72.
2. Its closing balance represents only work-in-progress and completed-but-unbilled jobs.
3. Its closing balance may also include the profit earned on workshop jobs.
Which of the statements are correct?

options.B: 1 and 2 only

e: WMS (Plan Head 72, Capital Suspense) holds expenditure only until outturn is billed; nothing except WIP and completed-but-unbilled work may remain in it — it is not a profit figure.

q:
Consider the following statements about the debit side of the WMS account:
1. Labour distributed from pay sheets through labour schedules is debited to WMS.
2. Material issued from the depot is debited to WMS at issue price.
3. Completed outturn transferred to final heads is debited to WMS.
4. On-cost absorbed into jobs is debited to WMS.
Which of the statements are correct?

options.B: 1, 3 and 4 only

e: Labour, material and absorbed on-cost are debits (cost flowing in); completed outturn is a credit, because it is expenditure flowing out of WMS to the final head.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Outturn Statement (W.1204):
1. Part I shows the outlay on works completed and adjustable in the month.
2. Part II shows the outlay on works in progress.
3. Part II also shows completed works awaiting adjustment or acceptance.
4. The amounts shown in Part I remain in WMS and form the closing balance.
Which of the statements are correct?

options.B: 2, 3 and 4 only

e: Part I amounts are credited out of WMS to final heads; it is the Part II amounts that stay in WMS and form the closing balance.

q:
Consider the following statements about on-cost in a workshop:
1. On-cost is absorbed into jobs at pre-determined percentages on direct labour.
2. Idle-time wages are charged to the Shop On-Cost Work Order.
3. On-cost rates are reviewed every quarter.
4. Depreciation of plant and buildings is kept apart as pro-forma on-cost.
Which of the statements are correct?

options.B: 1, 2 and 3 only

e: All four are correct: absorption is on direct labour (never on total cost), idle time goes to the shop on-cost work order, rates are reviewed quarterly, and depreciation is a pro-forma on-cost element kept apart.

q:
Consider the following statements about workshop costing records:
1. The Outturn Statement (W.1204) is prepared by the WAO and posted every month from the Workshop General Register.
2. All charges on each work order are collected in the Workshop General Register (W.1201).
3. The Cost Sheet (W.934) totals labour, material and on-cost into the job cost and unit cost.
4. The Outturn Statement is prepared by the CWM from the stores priced ledger.
Which of the statements are correct?

options.B: 1 and 4 only

e: W.1204 is the WAO's monthly statement posted from the WGR (W.1201); the Cost Sheet (W.934) is struck by the Costing Section. Statement 4 is wrong on both the officer and the source.

q:
Consider the following statements about the credit side of the WMS account:
1. Completed outturn billed to Capital, DRF, Revenue Demands and Stores Suspense is credited to WMS.
2. Material returned to stores is credited to WMS at returned / scrap value.
3. Direct purchases by the CWM are credited to WMS.
4. The balance carried down represents work-in-progress and completed-but-unbilled jobs.
Which of the statements are correct?

options.B: 1, 2 and 4 only

e: Outturn and returns to stores are credits; direct purchases are a debit, because the material is bought straight for workshop activity.

q:
Consider the following statements about the WMS closing-balance norm and review:
1. The closing balance should be about 3% of gross credits in repair workshops.
2. The closing balance should be about 6% of gross credits in manufacturing workshops.
3. A heavy closing balance indicates that outturn is not being adjusted promptly.
4. The review of the Workshop Manufacturing Account and the WGR is put up quarterly to the FA&CAO.
Which of the statements are correct?

options.B: 2 and 3 only

e: All four are correct — the norm is 3% for repair and 6% for manufacturing workshops (not the other way round), and the quarterly review goes to the FA&CAO.

q: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense (WMS) is operated under which Plan Head?

options.B: Plan Head 51

e: WMS is Plan Head 72 (P.7200), under Capital Suspense; Plan Head 71 is Stores Suspense.

q: Who prepares the Outturn Statement, Form W.1204?

options.B: The Senior Section Engineer of the shop

e: The Outturn Statement (W.1204) is prepared by the WAO, posted every month from the Workshop General Register; in computerised workshops it is generated in WAMS through the WGR module.

q: The WMS closing balance at the end of a month consists of:

options.A: Work-in-progress, billed outturn and returned stores
options.B: Work-in-progress and completed-but-unbilled jobs only
options.C: Work-in-progress and material lying in the stores depot
options.D: Completed jobs already billed to final heads

e: Only what could not be billed by month-end stays in WMS: jobs still in progress and jobs finished but not yet billed or adjusted. Nothing else may remain.

q: On what base is on-cost absorbed into workshop jobs?

options.A: On the total cost of the job
options.B: On the direct labour charges of the job
options.C: On the direct material cost of the job
options.D: On the prime cost of the job

e: On-cost is collected on on-cost work orders and then absorbed at pre-determined percentages on direct labour — never on total cost or prime cost.

q: The Workshop Outturn Register, maintained in two parts corresponding to the Outturn Statement, is posted monthly from:

options.B: The pay sheets of the workshop

e: All charges on each work order are collected in the Workshop General Register (W.1201), and the Outturn Register / Outturn Statement is posted monthly from the WGR.

q: In the specimen WMS account for a month, stores issued to jobs amount to Rs 3,65,000 and material purchased directly by the CWM amounts to Rs 15,000. The subtotal of the material group on the debit side of WMS is:
e: The material group combines stores issued and direct/local purchases: Rs 3,65,000 + Rs 15,000 = Rs 3,80,000.

q: During a month, WMS is debited with labour Rs 2,90,000, materials Rs 3,65,000, direct purchases Rs 15,000 and on-cost absorbed Rs 1,70,000. The total fresh debits to WMS during the month (excluding the opening balance) are:
e: Fresh debits exclude the opening balance brought down; Rs 15,25,000 is the total of both sides of the account including that balance.

q: In Part I of an Outturn Statement, the four completed jobs together carry direct labour of Rs 2,13,000. On-cost is absorbed at 75% of direct labour (shop 60% + general 15%). The total on-cost shown in Part I is:
e: On-cost rides on direct labour: 75% of Rs 2,13,000 gives the on-cost column total of Part I.

q: In Part II of an Outturn Statement, the Capital head shows an opening balance of Rs 3,20,000, debits during the month of Rs 2,60,000 and outturn (credits) of Rs 2,00,000. The closing balance under the Capital head is:
e: Closing balance = opening balance + debits in the month - outturn credited in the month.

q: A manufacture job is costed with direct labour Rs 56,000 and direct material Rs 84,000. Shop on-cost is 60% and general on-cost is 15%, both on direct labour. The total (works) cost of the job is:
e: Prime cost is Rs 1,40,000; total on-cost at 75% of direct labour is Rs 42,000, giving a works cost of Rs 1,82,000.

q: A workshop's WMS account opens with a debit balance of Rs 4,20,000. Fresh debits during the month are Rs 5,30,000. Credits during the month are: completed outturn transferred Rs 4,10,000 and materials returned to stores Rs 20,000. The closing balance of WMS is:
e: Closing balance = opening balance + fresh debits - total credits (outturn + returns).

q: Part I of an Outturn Statement shows the POH of one passenger coach billed to the DRF, with labour Rs 85,000, material Rs 1,10,000 and on-cost Rs 63,750. The total cost at which this job is billed is:
e: The billed total is the sum of the labour, material and on-cost columns for the job; the on-cost of Rs 63,750 is itself 75% of the labour of Rs 85,000.

q: Which one of the following statements about WMS and outturn is NOT correct?

options.A: The Outturn Statement (W.1204) is posted every month from the Workshop General Register
options.B: On-cost is absorbed into jobs at a pre-determined percentage on the total cost of each job
options.C: The WMS Account Current (W.1215) is rendered monthly by the WAO for each workshop
options.D: Material returned to stores is credited to WMS at returned / scrap value

e: On-cost is absorbed as a percentage on direct labour, never on total cost; the other three statements are correct.

q: Which one of the following statements about the WMS closing balance is NOT correct?

options.A: It represents work-in-progress and completed-but-unbilled jobs
options.B: It should be about 3% of gross credits in a repair workshop
options.C: It includes jobs completed and already billed to final heads during the month
options.D: A heavy closing balance shows that outturn is not being adjusted promptly

e: Jobs completed and billed have already been credited out of WMS through Part I of the Outturn Statement; they cannot form part of the closing balance.

q: Which one of the following statements about the Outturn Statement (W.1204) is NOT correct?

options.A: Part I shows works completed and adjustable in the month
options.B: Part II shows works in progress and completed works awaiting adjustment or acceptance
options.C: Vouchers received and accepted but not yet accounted for remain outstanding in Part II
options.D: Part II shows only those works which were completed and adjusted in the month

e: Completed-and-adjusted works belong to Part I. Part II covers work in progress and completed work awaiting adjustment/acceptance — saying it shows only completed-and-adjusted work reverses the two parts.

q: Which one of the following statements about idle time in a workshop is NOT correct?

options.A: Idle-time wages are charged directly to the job on which the worker was waiting
options.B: Idle time covers time lost waiting for material or work, machine breakdown and power failure
options.C: Idle time is charged to the Shop On-Cost Work Order
options.D: Idle time is absorbed over all jobs as part of on-cost

e: Charging idle time to a job is the classic wrong treatment: idle-time wages are never debited to a job; they go to the Shop On-Cost Work Order and spread over all jobs as on-cost.

q: Which one of the following statements about the closing-balance efficiency norm for WMS is NOT correct?

options.A: For repair workshops, the closing balance should be about 3% of gross credits
options.B: For manufacturing workshops, the closing balance should be about 6% of gross credits
options.C: For repair workshops, the closing balance should be about 6% of gross credits
options.D: The norm is expressed as the closing balance in relation to gross credits

e: The norm is 3% for repair workshops and 6% for manufacturing workshops; statement C reverses the repair-workshop figure.

q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.A: The review of the Workshop Manufacturing Account is put up quarterly to the FA&CAO
options.B: The WAO is administratively under the FA&CAO
options.C: One Squad Card serves the whole gang working together and is not issued worker-wise
options.D: The WAO is administratively under the CWM, whose workshop he accounts for

e: The WAO is administratively under the FA&CAO, not the CWM; budgetary control in the workshop rests with the CWE.

q: Which one of the following statements about material in the workshop is NOT correct?

options.A: Surplus material returned from the shop floor is credited to the job / WMS
options.B: Material purchased directly by the CWM must first pass through the Stores Suspense before it can be debited to WMS
options.C: Stores issued to a job are debited to the work order at issue price
options.D: Material purchased directly by the CWM is debited straight to WMS

e: Direct purchases by the CWM never pass through the Stores Suspense or the depot's priced ledger; they are debited straight to WMS.

q:
Assertion (A): Only work-in-progress and completed-but-unbilled jobs can remain in the closing balance of WMS.
Reason (R): Expenditure leaves WMS only when completed outturn is billed to the final head, or when material is returned to stores.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Both are true, and R explains A: since cost flows out of WMS only through billed outturn and returns to stores, whatever has not so left — WIP and completed-but-unbilled work — is all that can remain.

q:
Assertion (A): On-cost is absorbed into workshop jobs at pre-determined percentages on direct labour.
Reason (R): The on-cost percentages of shops are reviewed once a year, at the time of the annual budget.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: A is true — absorption is on direct labour at rates fixed in the On-Cost Budget. R is false — the percentages are reviewed quarterly, so that recovery keeps pace with actual overhead.
